title: Calculate with maxCost returns a within-budget distance that is far below the true distance
property: with maxCost>0, the result equals the exact distance if that is <= maxCost, otherwise it is a value > maxCost (a lower bound of the true distance)
input: Calculate("aaa", "bbbab", maxCost=2, insCost=1, subCost=2, delCost=2); also Similarity("aaa","bbbab", InsCost(1).SubCost(2).DelCost(2).MinScore(0.75))
expected: true distance is 6 > maxCost, so Calculate returns a value > 2 (e.g. 3); Similarity with MinScore 0.75 returns 0 (true score 0.25)
actual: Calculate returns 2 (looks like an exact in-budget distance); Similarity with MinScore 0.75 returns 0.75 instead of 0 (without MinScore it returns 0.25)
evidence: Docstring: 'If maxCost is non-zero, the calculation stops as soon as the distance is determined to be greater than maxCost. Therefore, any return value higher than maxCost is a lower bound for the actual distance.' Implied: a value <= maxCost is exact. Similarity/Match docs: scores lower than MinScore are returned as 0; here a 0.25 score is reported as 0.75.

title: Similarity/Match return NaN when the maximum possible distance is 0 due to zero costs
property: Similarity and Match always return a score in 0..1 for valid (non-negative) costs
input: Similarity("", "a", NewParams().InsCost(0)) and Match with the same params
actual: NaN (0/0, since maxDist is 0 and dist is 0)
evidence: Docs: 'The score is in the range of 0..1'; costs 'must be zero or positive' so 0 is explicitly allowed; the code comment shows the author intends to avoid divByZero issues but only guards the both-empty case.
